title: Dirty Electricity
author: Unknown
description: Dirty Electricity: Electrification and the Diseases of Civilization (second edition) by Samuel Milham, MD, MPH (iUniverse), an American epidemiologist known for early studies of cancer among electrical workers. Milham argues that many 'diseases of civilisation', including cardiovascular disease, cancer, diabetes and suicide, rose with the spread of electrification in the twentieth century. He draws on historical mortality data comparing electrified and unelectrified areas of the United States in the 1930s and 1940s, on his occupational studies, and on case reports of school and office clusters, to blame high-frequency voltage transients ('dirty electricity') on household wiring as well as other electromagnetic fields. The book also offers advice on measuring and reducing exposure. Its conclusions are contested by mainstream science, and it is part of the electromagnetic-health literature rather than an esoteric text.
